title: 389. The Fall of the Aztecs: The Night of Tears (Part 6)

sentences.en: It was midnight when Cortés gave the order to evacuate the palace.
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯下令撤离宫殿时，已是午夜时分。

sentences.en: A shroud of silence hung over the city.

sentences.en: Cortés had divided his company into three groups.

sentences.zh: 这支队伍中还有马林切和路易莎，以及马加里尼奥和他的工程师们，他们带着木制桥梁。

sentences.zh: 最后是阿尔瓦拉多和后卫部队，包括大部分骑兵。

sentences.en: Quietly, they moved through the streets, heading towards the western causeway.

sentences.zh: 当然，天花在欧洲随处可见。

sentences.en: So most of the Spaniards will have come into contact with it, although no people have come into contact with it.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数西班牙人都接触过它，尽管当地人从未接触过。

sentences.en: Many of them will have had smallpox scars.
sentences.zh: 他们中许多人身上都有天花留下的疤痕。

sentences.en: When Columbus and the first explorers and so on, when they arrived in Hispaniola, they brought smallpox with them.
sentences.zh: 当哥伦布和第一批探险家到达伊斯帕尼奥拉岛时，他们把天花也带去了。

sentences.en: It swept through the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 它席卷了整个加勒比地区。

sentences.en: And effectively, to be very simplistic, it wiped out, in the long run, virtually the entire Taino population.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，从长远来看，它几乎消灭了整个泰诺族人口。

sentences.en: And this is why it has, again, a kind of seismic impact because the Spaniards still need labour.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它再次产生了某种地震般的影响，因为西班牙人仍然需要劳动力。

sentences.en: And so they start looking to Africa for slaves.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始向非洲寻找奴隶。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They'd already used African slaves in the Canary Islands and the plantations there.
sentences.zh: 他们之前已经在加那利群岛和那里的种植园使用过非洲奴隶了。

sentences.en: Now they start to bring African slaves, which wasn't their original plan at all,
sentences.zh: 现在他们开始把非洲奴隶带过来，这根本不是他们最初的计划，

sentences.en: but they start to bring them to Hispaniola and Cuba and Jamaica and so on because they've run out of indigenous workers.
sentences.zh: 但因为当地劳动力耗尽，他们开始把奴隶带到伊斯帕尼奥拉岛、古巴、牙买加等地。

sentences.en: They haven't deliberately killed that workforce, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，他们并不是蓄意杀害那些劳动力。

sentences.en: So some people argue about genocide.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人对种族灭绝的说法有争议。

sentences.en: They didn't mean to kill them.
sentences.zh: 他们本意并非要杀害他们。

sentences.en: They wanted to keep them alive.
sentences.zh: 他们想让他们活着。

sentences.en: To work in their minds.
sentences.zh: 为了给他们干活。

sentences.en: To work in their minds, exactly.
sentences.zh: 为了给他们干活，没错。

sentences.en: Smallpox probably arrived in Mexico with Narbaez, not with Cortez, because there's no hint of it during Cortez's first journey.
sentences.zh: 天花很可能是随纳尔瓦埃斯而不是科尔特斯传入墨西哥的，因为科尔特斯的第一次远征中没有任何相关迹象。

sentences.en: Because basically all you need is a little scab on a cloak or something, and that's enough.
sentences.zh: 因为基本上你只需要斗篷上的一点结痂之类的东西就足够了。

sentences.en: You just need one person.
sentences.zh: 只需要一个人就够了。

sentences.en: One person.
sentences.zh: 一个人。

sentences.en: There's a story.
sentences.zh: 有个说法。

sentences.en: People have kind of fingered a culprit, an African porter called Francisco Eguia, but who knows if that's true or not, or whether it's actually, I mean,
sentences.zh: 人们似乎认定了一个罪魁祸首，一个叫弗朗西斯科·埃吉亚的非洲搬运工，但谁知道这是不是真的，或者是否其实……我是说，

sentences.en: it's very convenient they blame an African porter rather than a Spaniard.
sentences.zh: 把责任推给一个非洲搬运工而不是西班牙人，这太方便了。

sentences.en: What's not in doubt, though, is that the people of Mexico have no immunity to smallpox at all.
sentences.zh: 不过毫无疑问的是，墨西哥人对天花完全没有免疫力。

sentences.en: So once it's arrived in Narbaez's party, it spreads around the coast, village after village.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦它随纳尔瓦埃斯的队伍抵达，它就沿着海岸蔓延，村庄一个接一个地沦陷。

sentences.en: There are stories of villages deserted, of kind of jackals and vultures feasting on the remains of the people in these towns where literally everybody has died.
sentences.zh: 有报道称村庄荒废，豺狼和秃鹫在这些几乎所有人都死光的城镇里啃食遗体。

sentences.en: As one chronicler puts it, everything fell apart and it falls apart because these are communities, as in Europe, that depend on the harvest,
sentences.zh: 正如一位编年史家所言，一切都崩溃了，而崩溃的原因是这些社区和欧洲一样，依赖于收成，

sentences.en: that depend on there being a regular workforce.
sentences.zh: 依赖于稳定的劳动力。

sentences.en: And if there's no one to sow and to reap and to grind, you've got no food.
sentences.zh: 如果没有人播种、收割和研磨，就没有食物。

sentences.en: So people start to starve on top of that.
sentences.zh: 所以人们在瘟疫之上又开始挨饿。

sentences.en: People are starving on the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 人们在海岸上忍饥挨饿。

sentences.en: So by the way, when more Spaniards arrive, they find the coast deserted, the people weak and desperate, easy pickings.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，当更多的西班牙人抵达时，他们发现海岸荒无人烟，人们虚弱绝望，成了唾手可得的猎物。

sentences.en: No one to stop them arriving and more Spaniards arrive by sea.
sentences.zh: 没有人阻止他们登陆，更多的西班牙人从海上赶来。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, it's heading inland.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，疫情正向内陆蔓延。

sentences.en: By late September, smallpox has arrived in Tlaxcala, where it kills about a third of the population, probably.
sentences.zh: 到九月下旬，天花已抵达特拉斯卡拉，可能杀死了约三分之一的人口。

sentences.en: And so that must rebalance then the relationship between Cortez and the Tlaxcala.
sentences.zh: 那这必然会重新平衡科尔特斯与特拉斯卡拉人之间的关系。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Definitely, Tom.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And then it starts to move.
sentences.zh: 然后它开始移动。

sentences.en: Of course, it is carried further west into the Valley of Mexico, across the lake and into Tenochtitlan.
sentences.zh: 当然，它被带到了更西边的墨西哥谷，穿过湖泊，进入了特诺奇蒂特兰。

sentences.en: So in Tenochtitlan itself, what has happened after the Noche Trees Day?
sentences.zh: 那么在“悲伤之夜”之后，特诺奇蒂特兰城内发生了什么？

sentences.en: We don't really know what the Mexica are thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们并不真正了解墨西加人在想什么。

sentences.en: Well, they must be thinking, ah, God, they got away.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们一定在想，天哪，他们逃掉了。

sentences.en: But some of them maybe think, we've taught them a lesson they won't be back.
sentences.zh: 但有些人可能认为，我们给了他们教训，他们不会再回来了。

sentences.en: Some of them may fear they will be back.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能担心他们会回来。

sentences.en: I mean, who knows?
sentences.zh: 我是说，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I think they must be thinking, we've goofed.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们一定在想，我们搞砸了。

sentences.en: Do you think so?
sentences.zh: 你这么认为吗？

sentences.en: The whole point was to wipe them out.
sentences.zh: 重点本应是彻底消灭他们。

sentences.en: If they escape, you know, they know how dangerous they are.
sentences.zh: 如果他们逃脱了，你知道，他们知道这些人有多危险。

sentences.en: And don't forget, they killed two thirds of them.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，他们杀死了他们三分之二的人。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But I think that anyone who's seen what the Spaniards are capable of will know that it's not good for them still to be out there.
sentences.zh: 但我认为任何见过西班牙人能力的人都会知道，让他们继续在外面游荡对他们没好处。

sentences.en: Which is presumably why Kuitla Huac, who is the new emperor, who is Montezuma's brother, who has taken over, why he sent a message to Tlaxcala saying,
sentences.zh: 这大概就是为什么新皇帝奎特拉瓦克，也就是蒙特祖马的兄弟，在接管政权后，向特拉斯卡拉传话的原因，他说：

sentences.en: let's team up and get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 让我们联手除掉他们。

sentences.en: However, Kuitla Huac, about whom we know almost nothing, because he lasted about 80 days as emperor, because he gets smallpox.
sentences.zh: 然而，关于奎特拉瓦克我们几乎一无所知，因为他只当了大约80天的皇帝，因为他染上了天花。

sentences.en: Smallpox, of course, doesn't discriminate between rich and poor.
sentences.zh: 天花当然不分贫富。

sentences.en: We have Nahuatl accounts of sores breaking out on people's heads, people lying in their beds as if they were dead, unable even to lift their heads.
sentences.zh: 我们有纳瓦特尔语的记载，描述人们头上长出疮，躺在床上像死了一样，甚至连头都抬不起来。

sentences.en: When they moved at all, they screamed in pain.
sentences.zh: 当他们稍微动弹时，就会痛得尖叫。

sentences.en: Many died from the plague, but others died from hunger.
sentences.zh: 许多人死于瘟疫，但也有人死于饥饿。

sentences.en: They were too weak to look for food, while everybody else was too ill to care for them.
sentences.zh: 他们太虚弱了，无法寻找食物，而其他人也病得无法照顾他们。

sentences.en: So they starved to death where they lay.
sentences.zh: 于是他们就这样躺着饿死了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like if Europe, while it was being hit by the Black Death, suddenly got invaded by, I don't know, the Chinese.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就像欧洲在遭受黑死病袭击时，突然被，我不知道，被中国人入侵了一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly it, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 没错，就是这样，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: The effect on Mexica society.
sentences.zh: 这对墨西加社会的影响。

sentences.en: I mean, the trauma, the arrival of the Spaniards.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那种创伤，西班牙人的到来。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: The death of Montezuma, the death of his brother, who's just taken over as emperor, the spread of this plague.
sentences.zh: 蒙特祖马的死，他刚继位为皇帝的兄弟的死，这场瘟疫的蔓延。

sentences.en: I mean, they must be in shock.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们一定处于震惊之中。

sentences.en: And actually, they're fortunate in some ways that the next emperor, who is Montezuma's cousin, the next guy to be chosen is called Cuauhtémoc.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们某种程度上很幸运，下一任皇帝，也就是蒙特祖马的堂弟，被选中的人叫夸特莫克。

sentences.en: So this is the guy that we mentioned in the previous episode as a possible culprit in the killing of Moctezuma.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们在上一集提到的，可能是杀害蒙特祖马的嫌疑人之一。

sentences.en: I mean, almost certainly not, but...
sentences.zh: 我是说，几乎肯定不是，但是……

sentences.en: He's a Spaniard skeptic, I think it's fair to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以公平地说，他是一个西班牙怀疑论者，汤姆。

sentences.en: He's always been very suspicious of them.
sentences.zh: 他一直对他们非常警惕。

sentences.en: He is clearly a very formidable person.
sentences.zh: 他显然是一个非常可怕的人。

sentences.en: On his first day as emperor, he rounds up six of Montezuma's sons and he has them executed.
sentences.zh: 在他当皇帝的第一天，他就把蒙特祖马的六个儿子抓起来处决了。

sentences.en: Very kind of Ottoman behavior, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 这很像奥斯曼帝国的行径，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: It gets rid of all the competition.
sentences.zh: 这消除了所有的竞争对手。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not just competition also, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这不仅仅是为了消除竞争。

sentences.en: It's the kind of the doves.
sentences.zh: 这是一种鸽派的清除。

sentences.en: So his name actually means Falling Eagle, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以他的名字其实意味着“坠落的鹰”，对吧？

sentences.en: He's very much a hawk, one might say.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会说，他非常像一只鹰派。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Montezuma's sons were much more dovish in their attitude towards the Spaniards.
sentences.zh: 而蒙特祖马的儿子们对西班牙人的态度要温和得多。

sentences.en: So by getting rid of them, he's not just getting rid of rivals, he's also getting rid of political opposition.
sentences.zh: 所以通过除掉他们，他不仅是在消除竞争对手，也是在消除政治反对派。

sentences.en: Of appeasers.
sentences.zh: 消除绥靖派。

sentences.en: Of appeasers, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，消除绥靖派。

sentences.en: And then he marries Montezuma's daughter, Tocquech Potsin.
sentences.zh: 然后他娶了蒙特祖马的女儿托克切波钦。

sentences.en: So the very girl, the hostage, who looked like she might have died in the Night of Tears.
sentences.zh: 就是那个在“悲伤之夜”中看起来可能已经死掉的人质女孩。

sentences.en: Actually, she didn't die.
sentences.zh: 其实她没死。

sentences.en: She was rescued from the lake by Mexica, recognized, taken back to the court.
sentences.zh: 她被墨西加人从湖中救起，被认出来后带回了宫廷。

sentences.en: And Cuauhtémoc marries her.
sentences.zh: 然后夸特莫克娶了她。

sentences.en: So that's a way of uniting the various branches of the family.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种团结家族各分支的方式。

sentences.en: It's very Henry Tudor after the Battle of Bosworth, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很像博斯沃思战役后的亨利·都铎，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he's in charge, and he seems to be an impressive guy, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以他掌权了，而且他看起来确实是个令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: There's no reason to doubt that he's quite a formidable person.
sentences.zh: 没有理由怀疑他是一个相当可怕的人。

sentences.en: However, not only is he facing the smallpox, he's also facing a campaign the like of which the Mexica have never seen before,
sentences.zh: 然而，他不仅面临天花，还面临着墨西加人从未见过的战役，

sentences.en: because the conquistadors are determined to wage a European-style war.
sentences.zh: 因为征服者们决心发动一场欧洲式的战争。

sentences.en: And Cortez's strategy is very clever.
sentences.zh: 而且科尔特斯的策略非常聪明。

sentences.en: So you mentioned Terra, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你提到了特拉，汤姆。

sentences.en: The first target is a hill town called Tepeyaca.
sentences.zh: 第一个目标是一个叫特佩亚卡的山城。

sentences.en: And that commands the trade route from the Valley of Mexico to the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 它控制着从墨西哥谷到海岸的贸易路线。

sentences.en: Because, Dominic, the size of the city means that it is dependent on imports.
sentences.zh: 因为，多米尼克，这座城市的规模意味着它依赖进口。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it's going to starve.
sentences.zh: 否则它就会挨饿。

sentences.en: It's always been unusual, actually, Tenochtitlan, because it doesn't have lots of farmlands of its own.
sentences.zh: 事实上，特诺奇蒂特兰一直很特别，因为它没有多少自己的农田。

sentences.en: So they do have these floating gardens, but it's in a lake.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实有那些浮动花园，但它是在湖里的。

sentences.en: So they've always depended on tribute payments from other places.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一直依赖其他地方的贡品。

sentences.en: And actually, one argument for the rise of the Aztecs is that because they didn't have farmlands, they didn't have to spend lots of time faffing around with the harveSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，关于阿兹特克人崛起的一个论点是，因为他们没有农田，他们不必花大量时间在收成上瞎忙活。

sentences.en: No, like the Spartans.
sentences.zh: 没错，就像斯巴达人一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: They were freer to go off and fight people.
sentences.zh: 他们能更自由地去出征作战。

sentences.en: Well, Tepeyaca commands this really important trade route.
sentences.zh: 特佩亚卡（Tepeyaca）控制着一条非常重要的贸易路线。

sentences.en: Cortez hits that first, but he hits it in an absolutely ruthless, gruesome way.
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯首先攻打那里，但他采取了极其残忍、恐怖的手段。

sentences.en: You astound me.
sentences.zh: 你让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: All the women and children are rounded up and they have the letter G stamped on their cheeks with a red hot brand, meaning war, Jif Higeta, and they are sold as slaves.
sentences.zh: 所有的妇女和儿童都被抓了起来，他们的脸颊上被烙上了红热的“G”字印记，代表“战争”（Guerra），然后被当作奴隶卖掉。

sentences.en: The surviving men are dragged back to Tlashkala to be sacrificed, and the story goes that others are torn apart by dogs.
sentences.zh: 幸存的男子被拖回特拉斯卡拉（Tlashkala）充当祭品，还有传言说其他人被狗撕成了碎片。

sentences.en: And there are even rumours that they are chopped up in butcher shops before being feasted on by the Tlashkalaans in the victory banquet.
sentences.zh: 甚至有传言说，他们在胜利宴会上被特拉斯卡拉人吃掉之前，先在屠宰场里被肢解了。

sentences.en: Now, of course, some of these stories may be wildly exaggerated or completely untrue.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中一些故事可能被严重夸大了，或者完全不属实。

sentences.en: But it doesn't redound to the Spanish credit, does it?
sentences.zh: 但这并不能为西班牙人增光，不是吗？

sentences.en: No, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 确实不能。

sentences.en: You know, that their allies are doing this.
sentences.zh: 毕竟是他们的盟友在做这些事。

sentences.en: Cortez would say, you know what Cortez would say if he came as an unexpected guest on the rest of this history?
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯会说——你知道如果科尔特斯作为这段历史的意外访客，他会怎么说吗？

sentences.en: He would say, listen, mate, I wasn't playing badminton on a Sunday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 他会说：听着，伙计，我可不是在周日下午打羽毛球。

sentences.en: Yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 是啊，没错。

sentences.en: But I mean, he'd be, you know, doing the slaughter.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，他当时就在那儿，你知道的，在进行屠杀。

sentences.en: That's what you have to do.
sentences.zh: 那是你必须做的事。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the way it is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: But sacrificing people to demons and eating them in victory feasts, no Christian is going to boast about doing that or even admit that he's been complicit in it.
sentences.zh: 但把人献祭给恶魔并在胜利宴会上吃掉他们，没有哪个基督徒会以此为荣，甚至不会承认自己参与其中。

sentences.en: So where are those stories coming from?
sentences.zh: 那么这些故事是从哪儿来的呢？

sentences.en: That's a good question, actually, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个好问题，汤姆。

sentences.en: Where are those stories coming from?
sentences.zh: 这些故事是从哪儿来的呢？

sentences.en: Some of those stories are from indigenous sources.
sentences.zh: 其中一些故事来自原住民的记载。

sentences.en: So it could be Mexica.
sentences.zh: 所以可能是墨西加人（Mexica）的说法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Anti-Tlashkala propaganda.
sentences.zh: 反特拉斯卡拉的宣传。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, I think there are hints of these stories in some of the Spanish accounts, actually.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为在一些西班牙人的记载中，其实也有这些故事的蛛丝马迹。

sentences.en: The Spanish accounts don't really stint on the brutality.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人的记载并没有掩盖其残暴性。

sentences.en: No, but I'm just saying that there's a qualitative difference between the kind of brutality that you'd wage in a European war and human sacrifice and cannibalism.
sentences.zh: 不，我只是说，你在欧洲战争中进行的残暴行为与活人祭祀和食人行为之间存在本质区别。

sentences.en: There is, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想确实有。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a fine distinction, though, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，这只是细微的差别，不是吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: It's all right to massacre loads of people, but not to eat them?
sentences.zh: 屠杀大量人口是可以的，但吃掉他们就不行？

sentences.en: No, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不行。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, in the European context, killing people in battle is one thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，在欧洲背景下，战场上杀人是一回事。

sentences.en: Eating them and sacrificing them to demons is unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 把他们吃掉并献祭给恶魔是不可接受的。

sentences.en: It's crossing a line, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 这越界了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, that's where you and I would just have to disagree, Tom, because I think...
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是我和你必须持不同意见的地方，汤姆，因为我认为……

sentences.en: You know, I'm not saying that as a kind of moralist or a philosopher.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我并不是以某种道德家或哲学家的身份这么说。

sentences.en: As a wokeSt.
sentences.zh: 以“觉醒派”的身份。

sentences.en: No, I'm saying that in the context of Christian culture...
sentences.zh: 不，我是说在基督教文化的背景下……

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是啊，当然。

sentences.en: I know what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 我知道你想说什么。

sentences.en: Sacrificing people to demons.
sentences.zh: 把人献祭给恶魔。

sentences.en: I know what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 我知道你想说什么。

sentences.en: Well, stop.
sentences.zh: 好了，停下。

sentences.en: You're saying, how does Cortez square that?
sentences.zh: 你是说，科尔特斯怎么能接受这一点？

sentences.en: I'm not even saying that, because Cortez has to lump it, because he knows he has to deal with his allies.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不是那个意思，因为科尔特斯只能忍气吞声，因为他知道他必须与盟友打交道。

sentences.en: I'm just saying that it's not beyond the bounds of possibility that those things actually happened, because the Christians have no stake in propagating stories like that.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，这些事情确实发生过并非不可能，因为基督徒没有理由去传播这样的故事。

sentences.en: Oh, I agree with you completely, by the way.
sentences.zh: 哦，顺便说一句，我完全同意你的看法。

sentences.en: I totally agree with you.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意你。

sentences.en: That's all I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我就是这个意思。

sentences.en: In Cortez's letters and so on, he downplays the involvement of the Tlaxcala.
sentences.zh: 在科尔特斯的信件等等中，他淡化了特拉斯卡拉人的参与。

sentences.en: Yeah, he doesn't want to mention that.
sentences.zh: 是的，他不想提及这一点。

sentences.en: So not only Tlaxcala, but later on, they'll have another ally in Texcoco, and that's very important as well in taking control of the lake.
sentences.zh: 所以不仅是特拉斯卡拉，后来他们还有了另一个盟友——特斯科科（Texcoco），这在控制湖区方面也非常重要。

sentences.en: And again, that's often lost, not just in the Spaniards' own accounts, but in later kind of romantic versions of the story,
sentences.zh: 而且这一点经常被忽略，不仅是在西班牙人自己的记载中，在后来的一些浪漫化的故事版本中也是如此，

sentences.en: the kind of William Prescott in the 19th century or something, where it's seen as Spaniards versus Aztecs.
sentences.zh: 比如19世纪威廉·普雷斯科特（William Prescott）的作品，在那里它被看作是西班牙人与阿兹特克人的对决。

sentences.en: It was never like that.
sentences.zh: 事实从来不是那样。

sentences.en: Spaniards were always outnumbered by their indigenous allies.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人的人数总是少于他们的原住民盟友。

sentences.en: But more Hispanians are starting to arrive, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但越来越多的西班牙人开始抵达了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we're in late 1520 now, and there are ships arriving from Cuba, Hispaniola, even from Spain all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在处于1520年底，不断有船只从古巴、伊斯帕尼奥拉岛，甚至从西班牙抵达。

sentences.en: And they're bringing supplies of guns and crossbows and horses.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了枪支、弩和马匹的补给。

sentences.en: But above all, they are bringing more and more people.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，他们带来了越来越多的人。

sentences.en: And so what is Cortes' status vis-a-vis Velázquez and Charles V back in Spain now?
sentences.zh: 那么科尔特斯现在相对于委拉斯开兹（Velázquez）和西班牙国王查理五世（Charles V）的地位如何？

sentences.en: This is still very uncertain.
sentences.zh: 这仍然非常不确定。

sentences.en: Nothing has legally been settled.
sentences.zh: 法律上没有任何定论。

sentences.en: So Cortes is actually pursuing this enterprise without any form, really, of legal sanction.
sentences.zh: 所以科尔特斯实际上是在没有任何法律许可的情况下进行这项事业的。

sentences.en: He's got the stuff about the town.
sentences.zh: 他有关于那个城镇的文件。

sentences.en: You know, I've just been appointed by the town council of Vera Cruz.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我刚刚被维拉克鲁斯（Vera Cruz）市议会任命。

sentences.en: That was his claim.
sentences.zh: 那是他的主张。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But he doesn't have any letter from the king saying, you are the governor, you are the viceroy, anything like that.
sentences.zh: 但他没有任何来自国王的信件说：你是总督，你是副王，或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: So the people who are coming, these are-
sentences.zh: 所以那些来的人，他们是——

sentences.en: Glory hunters.
sentences.zh: 追名逐利之徒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Glory hunters, entrepreneurial fighters.
sentences.zh: 追名逐利之徒，投机取巧的战士。

sentences.en: But presumably, I mean, you know, the wisdom of the crowds, they think, yeah, we're onto a good thing here.
sentences.zh: 但大概，你知道，群众的智慧，他们会想，是的，我们碰上了好机会。

sentences.en: They do, of course.
sentences.zh: 他们当然会这么想。

sentences.en: We can make money.
sentences.zh: 我们可以赚钱。

sentences.en: Now, a key part of this story, if we just move thousands of miles east, Charles V, the great king of Spain, but also the emperor, ruler of huge swathes of Europe,
sentences.zh: 现在，这个故事的一个关键部分，如果我们向东移动几千英里，查理五世，伟大的西班牙国王，同时也是皇帝，统治着欧洲大片领土，

sentences.en: is in the Low Countries, sort of proceeding around.
sentences.zh: 当时正在低地国家巡游。

sentences.en: And with him, he has brought the gold that Cortes originally sent back.
sentences.zh: 他随身带着科尔特斯最初送回来的黄金。

sentences.en: And his men have put it on as an exhibition in Brussels Town Hall.
sentences.zh: 他的人把这些黄金放在布鲁塞尔市政厅展出。

sentences.en: Magnificent, late medieval kind of Renaissance building.
sentences.zh: 那是一座宏伟的中世纪晚期文艺复兴风格建筑。

sentences.en: On the 27th of August, 1520.
Oh, this is Albrecht Dürer.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是阿尔布雷特·丢勒（Albrecht Dürer）。

sentences.en: A young man called Albrecht Dürer.
sentences.zh: 一个叫阿尔布雷特·丢勒的年轻人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Goes to see it.
sentences.zh: 去看了展览。

sentences.en: And he's blown away, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他被震撼了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: An extraordinary account.
sentences.zh: 一段非凡的记录。

sentences.en: I saw the things which had been brought to the king from the new land of gold.
sentences.zh: 我看到了从新金地带给国王的东西。

sentences.en: I saw a sun, all of gold, a whole fathom broad, a moon, all of silver of the same size, two rooms of armor, and all manner of wondrous weapons, very strange clothing,
sentences.zh: 我看到了一个纯金的太阳，足有一噚那么宽，一个同样大小的纯银月亮，两间盔甲，以及各种奇妙的武器、非常奇怪的服装，

sentences.en: and all kinds of wonderful objects.
sentences.zh: 还有各种各样的奇妙物品。

sentences.en: All the days of my life, I have seen nothing that rejoiced my heart so much as these things, for I saw among them wonderful works of art,
sentences.zh: 我一生中从未见过像这些东西一样让我心花怒放的，因为我在其中看到了奇妙的艺术品，

sentences.en: and I marveled at the subtle ingenuity of men in foreign lands.
sentences.zh: 我惊叹于异国人民那精巧的创造力。

sentences.en: I mean, I wonder about that word ingenuity.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我对“创造力”（ingenuity）这个词感到好奇。

sentences.en: I wonder if it's coming from Ingenio.
sentences.zh: 我想知道它是否源自“Ingenio”。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which would perhaps more properly be described as genius, so the genius of a people.
sentences.zh: 这或许更准确地描述为“天才”（genius），也就是一个民族的天才。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's often left in the original.
sentences.zh: 它通常保留在原文中。

sentences.en: I think ingenuity downplays it.
sentences.zh: 我认为“创造力”这个词低估了它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I think it's recognising this is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是在承认这非常了不起。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not just that they're ingenious.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不仅仅是他们很聪明。

sentences.en: They have a distinctive quality that we would never have guessed.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有一种我们从未猜到过的独特品质。

sentences.en: I think you're absolutely right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我想你是完全正确的，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think Dürer is completely blown away by it.
sentences.zh: 我认为丢勒完全被它震撼了。

sentences.en: I think most people in Europe are stunned and staggered.
sentences.zh: 我认为欧洲的大多数人都感到震惊和错愕。

sentences.en: I think it gives the lie, actually, that passage to the idea that people in Europe immediately saw the peoples of the new world as backwards and as lesser.
sentences.zh: 我认为这段文字实际上驳斥了那种认为欧洲人立即将新世界的人民视为落后和低人一等的观点。

sentences.en: Because Dürer certainly doesn't...
sentences.zh: 因为丢勒肯定没有……

sentences.en: I think they had done, hadn't they, with the Tainos?
sentences.zh: 我想他们之前确实是这样认为的，不是吗，对泰诺人（Tainos）？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I think the general feeling of disappointment.
sentences.zh: 我想那是一种普遍的失望感。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the revelation of these treasures and then the reports coming back saying, you know, it's better than Venice, I guess that is changing.
sentences.zh: 但这些宝藏的揭示，以及随后传回的报告说，你知道，这比威尼斯还要好，我想这正在改变。

sentences.en: Definitely it is.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So this is a qualitative difference from the stuff that was coming back in the 1490s.
sentences.zh: 所以这与1490年代传回的东西有着本质的区别。

sentences.en: This blows people's minds.
sentences.zh: 这让人们大开眼界。

sentences.en: It's like you've discovered an alien civilisation and it's, you know, it's not some sort of Beatles kind of messing around in rock formations.
sentences.zh: 就像你发现了一个外星文明，你知道，这可不是什么披头士乐队在岩层里瞎搞。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Blobs of amoeba.
sentences.zh: 变形虫的团块。

sentences.en: This is a glittering city and, of course, when people see this and the word spreads, people are printing reports of it and writing letters to each other, very excited.
sentences.zh: 这是一座闪闪发光的城市，当然，当人们看到这些，消息传开后，人们印刷相关报告并互相写信，非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Of course, loads of people are going to pile in.
sentences.zh: 当然，会有很多人蜂拥而至。

sentences.en: Hundreds and then thousands.
sentences.zh: 成百上千，然后是成千上万。

sentences.en: Isn't there also, there's a report that appears, so this is the first illustration of Tenochtitlan in any European source.
sentences.zh: 难道没有一份报告出现吗？这是欧洲文献中第一次出现特诺奇蒂特兰（Tenochtitlan）的插图。

sentences.en: I think it's published in Nuremberg.
sentences.zh: 我想它是在纽伦堡出版的。

sentences.en: Yeah, Nuremberg.
sentences.zh: 是的，纽伦堡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And it's part of a newsletter that is set out by the bankers in Nuremberg.
sentences.zh: 它是纽伦堡银行家们发出的通讯的一部分。

sentences.en: So they are obviously immediately waking up.
sentences.zh: 所以他们显然立刻就警觉起来了。

sentences.en: You know, it's probably not the artistic quality of the metal work that's appealing to them, but the fact that it glitters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，吸引他们的可能不是金属工艺的艺术价值，而是它闪闪发光的事实。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So they know what is out there.
sentences.zh: 所以他们知道外面有什么。

sentences.en: And so all of which presumably is fueling enthusiasm, not just in the West Indies, but in Europe for people to go out there.
sentences.zh: 所有这些大概都在激发人们的热情，不仅是在西印度群岛，在欧洲也是如此，人们都想去那里。

sentences.en: Absolutely, Tom.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样，汤姆。

sentences.en: And they are going to bring those two things for which the indigenous peoples are completely repaired.
sentences.zh: 他们将带去两样东西，而原住民对此毫无防备。

sentences.en: One of them is the weaponry.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是武器。

sentences.en: So the swords, the guns, all that business.
sentences.zh: 剑、枪，所有那些东西。

sentences.en: The cannon.
sentences.zh: 大炮。

sentences.en: And they're going to bring germs and more viruses that will cause enormous damage to the peoples of the Americas.
sentences.zh: 他们还将带去病菌和更多的病毒，这将对美洲人民造成巨大的伤害。

sentences.en: So let's get to Christmas 1520, end of the year.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们进入1520年的圣诞节，也就是年底。

sentences.en: Cortez spends the winter back in Tlaxcala.
sentences.zh: 科尔特斯在特拉斯卡拉度过了那个冬天。

sentences.en: He's already started to knock out some of the towns and cities that are loyal to Tenochtitlan.
sentences.zh: 他已经开始着手攻打那些效忠于特诺奇蒂特兰的城镇和城市了。

sentences.en: We can't, we're not obviously going to go through them all.
sentences.zh: 我们显然不可能一一细说。

sentences.en: He has cut most of Tenochtitlan's links to the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 他已经切断了特诺奇蒂特兰通往海岸的大部分联系。

sentences.en: And his plan is very clear.
sentences.zh: 他的计划非常明确。

sentences.en: He will strangle the heartland of the Mexica, of the Aztec Empire.
sentences.zh: 他要扼杀墨西加人，也就是阿兹特克帝国的核心地带。

sentences.en: He will confine them to the lake.
sentences.zh: 他要把他们困在湖中。

sentences.en: He will win control of the lake towns.
sentences.zh: 他要夺取对湖畔城镇的控制权。

sentences.en: He will cut off their supplies of food and water.
sentences.zh: 他要切断他们的食物和水源供应。

sentences.en: So this is completely different from the campaigns that the Aztecs are used to fighting.
sentences.zh: 所以，这与阿兹特克人习惯的战争方式完全不同。

sentences.en: They're used to those flower wars.
sentences.zh: 他们习惯的是那种“花之战”。

sentences.en: These ritualized, almost, they're kind of sacral, aren't they, Tom?
sentences.zh: 那种仪式化的，甚至可以说是神圣的，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: People dressing up as owls.
sentences.zh: 人们打扮成猫头鹰的样子。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Something about that.
sentences.zh: 确实有那么回事。

sentences.en: Yeah, we'll be coming back to people dressing up as owls later on.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们稍后会再谈到人们打扮成猫头鹰的事。

sentences.en: I love an episode that features someone dressing up as an owl.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那种有角色打扮成猫头鹰的剧集。

sentences.en: So they are used to these campaigns where you take prisoners for sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 所以他们习惯的是那种为了抓俘虏献祭而进行的战争。

sentences.en: Not where you starve people out and you fight over months and months, a very long campaign, a European-style campaign.
sentences.zh: 而不是那种通过围困把人饿死，持续数月之久的长期战争，那种欧洲式的战争。

sentences.en: A war of attrition.
sentences.zh: 一场消耗战。

sentences.en: And this is Cortez's plan.
sentences.zh: 这就是科尔特斯的计划。

sentences.en: And Tlaxcala are kind of happy to go along with it.
sentences.zh: 而特拉斯卡拉人也乐于配合。

sentences.en: They have their own internal issues because, of course, they've got smallpox.
sentences.zh: 他们自己内部也有问题，因为当然了，他们也染上了天花。

sentences.en: They have some faction fighting.
sentences.zh: 他们内部也有派系斗争。

sentences.en: But basically, they go along with him.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，他们还是听从了他的安排。

sentences.en: The story goes that on the 27th of December, Cortez prepares to go for phase two.
sentences.zh: 据记载，12月27日，科尔特斯准备开启第二阶段。

sentences.en: He gathers his men in the main temple in Tlaxcala.
sentences.zh: 他在特拉斯卡拉的主神庙召集了他的部下。

sentences.en: And he says, as you would expect he would, he says, this is a great crusade.
sentences.zh: 他发表了演说，正如你所预料的那样，他说这是一场伟大的十字军东征。

sentences.en: We're going to win Mexico for Christ and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们要为基督赢得墨西哥，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And then a rare moment of honesty.
sentences.zh: 然后，他罕见地流露出了诚实的一面。

sentences.en: He says, it just so happens that this campaign will bring us both honor and profit.
sentences.zh: 他说，恰好这场战役既能给我们带来荣誉，也能带来利益。

sentences.en: Two things that very rarely go together.
sentences.zh: 这两者很少能兼得。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, that's Cortez.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是科尔特斯。

sentences.en: To me in a nutshell, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就是他的本质，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, on New Year's Eve, they hit the town of Texcoco, which is the second city of the Aztec Triple Alliance.
sentences.zh: 所以，在除夕夜，他们袭击了特斯科科，那是阿兹特克三方同盟的第二大城市。

sentences.en: There's a whole issue with a massive succession crisis that's been going on in Texcoco.
sentences.zh: 特斯科科当时正陷入一场大规模的继承危机，问题重重。

sentences.en: Don't go there, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 别提那个了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm not going to go there.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我不提那个了。

sentences.en: I actually find it very hard to follow.
